title: Penne alla Vodka
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Penne alla Vodka combines tomato and cream into a blush-pink sauce, with a splash of vodka that heightens the tomato's flavor without leaving any boozy taste behind.
longDesc: A relatively modern addition to the Italian pasta canon, rising to popularity in the 1970s-80s, this dish relies on vodka to help release flavor compounds in the tomato that are only soluble in alcohol, resulting in a rounder, more complex sauce than tomato and cream alone.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the penne until al dente.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil and butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and red pepper flakes, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the vodka and simmer for 2–3 minutes to cook off most of the alcohol, scraping up any browned bits.
Add the crushed tomatoes and a pinch of salt, simmering for 12–15 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the cream and simmer for another 3–4 minutes until the sauce turns a pale pink and silky.
Drain the pasta and toss directly into the sauce, adding the Parmigiano and tossing to combine.
chefTips: Simmering the vodka for a few minutes cooks off most of the harsh alcohol taste while retaining its flavor-enhancing effect.
Add the cream at the end and avoid boiling it hard, to prevent the sauce from splitting.
A touch of tomato paste can deepen the color and flavor if your tomatoes are on the milder side.
commonMistakes: Skipping the vodka simmer time, leaving a harsh, boozy taste.
Boiling the sauce hard after adding cream, which can cause it to separate.
Using too little tomato, resulting in a sauce that's more cream than tomato.
storage: Refrigerate the sauce for up to 3 days.
reheating: Reheat gently over low heat, stirring, to avoid splitting the cream.
healthBenefits: A good source of lycopene from the tomatoes.
Best enjoyed in moderation given the cream and butter content.
culturalNote: Despite feeling like a timeless classic, Penne alla Vodka is a 20th-century invention, and its exact origin is disputed between Italy and Italian-American kitchens in the United States.
